page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and utilizes an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The server delivers 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no bundled local storage, meaning primary persistence requires network-attached cloud storage. Networking features a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and the instance operates without GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes locate the instance in lower relative performance brackets compared to contemporary infrastructure. Geekbench testing reports single-core and multi-core scores of 920.0 and 1996.0, while PassMark results include a CPU score of 3601.23 and a memory score of 1513.47. Memory throughput reaches 19.6 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 18.16 GB/sec for large write operations. In operational tests, the server completed Redis SET commands at 2.83 million operations per second and served static web data at 2.28 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs center around memory capacity versus compute throughput. While the 32 GB RAM allocation suits services requiring expanded working memory, processor and bandwidth measurements remain comparatively modest. In qualitative terms, the instance serves as a dedicated-core memory-dense environment where workload memory sizing is the primary constraint rather than raw CPU or I/O throughput. Workload fit includes caching layers, staging databases, lightweight in-memory stores, and background queue workers requiring high memory-to-core ratios.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture with a KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Baseline networking capability is 2 Gbps. Relative benchmark evaluations show modest CPU performance, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1996.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3601.23, while memory bandwidth achieves 19.6 GB/sec for uncached reads. Redis SET operations perform at 2.83 million operations per second. Given its high RAM allocation relative to compute capability, the ecs.se1ne.xlarge is best matched with memory-heavy workloads that do not demand high compute density, such as in-memory caches, small databases, and memory-constrained utility tasks.
